audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Volibear rows 1-5 with Skill at either end. The already-audited mirror (maokai__volibear) settled it as Level 1 Volibear, Levels 2-3 Maokai, Levels 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Maokai, First item and 2+ items Volibear.
audit.why: Maokai's laning tools all come online in that band: Bramble Smash on 7s, Twisted Advance's undodgeable root on 14s, and a 3000-range Nature's Grasp at 6. Volibear's stages are level 1 and the item phases, where his health and on-hit bites out-last a low-damage tank.
audit.corrected: Volibear, Maokai, Maokai, Skill, Maokai, Volibear, Volibear on both layers, ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Volibear's window ('R Stormbringer answers his all-in and out-bursts him') with no mention of Nature's Grasp.
audit.why: Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1 with 3000 range and roots everything in the advancing wall's path — it is exactly what punishes a 550-range leap that has to walk back out. Stormbringer's own tower disable stays a real dive enabler, but not into a healthy Maokai.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and whys[4] now state the 130s / 3000-range root as the reason level 6 is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contradicted itself in one field: 'His lock-on root. Dodge it.' followed by 'lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.' Riot's text says Maokai becomes untargetable and dashes to the target, rooting on arrival — there is nothing to sidestep. Sap Magic's heal-on-attack (refreshed by every spell cast or spell taken) was also never mentioned even though the page recommends Executioner's Calling.
audit.why: Telling a player to dodge an undodgeable root is worse than saying nothing: he will stand in range waiting to react. The answer is range, not reaction.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance is 14s / 525 range, untargetable during the dash, lock-on root — space outside 525 instead of trying to dodge; Bramble Smash is a 7s knockback and slow; Sap Magic is the heal Grievous Wounds answers.

audit.why: 'Fight in saplings' and 'Extend into his sustain' are the right common mistakes for this matchup — Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 and more effective in brush, and Sap Magic refunds his health through long trades.
audit.corrected: Kept; dontsFull[1].d replaced with a real reason instead of generic filler.

edits.before: Dodge his W root — Q-stun all-in his low damage. Volibear wins by trading around Maokai's Twisted Advance (Root) and cashing the pattern: dodge W and all-in his low damage.
edits.after: You cannot dodge his W — Twisted Advance is lock-on and he is untargetable mid-dash, so stay outside 525 until it is spent. Then Thundering Smash in and bite the mark twice for the heal.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Maokai Twisted Advance: Dashes to a target and roots them — lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (W): 14s at rank 1, 525 range — he is untargetable during the dash and the root is lock-on, so it cannot be dodged; space outside 525 instead. - Bramble Smash (Q): 7s knockback and slow.

edits.after: Lock-on root, undodgeable — stay outside 525 until he spends it.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The second Frenzied Maul on a marked target is your heal — no mark, no sustain.

edits.before: Q + W online — stun in, double-bite out. Maokai has to respect every walk-up once your second W heal-bite threatens.
edits.after: Q + W online, but Bramble Smash (7s at rank 1) knocks you back and slows — bite, then step out before it lands.

edits.before: E completes the pattern: shield yourself as you disengage or slow Maokai under the sky-splitter. This is the start of your kill window.
edits.after: Sky Splitter slows and shields you in the blast, but Twisted Advance is untargetable on the way in — his root beats your stun to the punch.

edits.before: W ranks make the wounded-bite chunk hard. Run Maokai down every time Twisted Advance (Root) is on cooldown — you win the stat-check from here to 6.
edits.after: W ranks make the wounded-bite chunk hard, but Sap Magic heals him back off every spell — even stage, so bite only in the 14s after Twisted Advance.

edits.before: Stormbringer online — you can dive Maokai under tower with the disable. The 3-6 window is the strongest your lane will ever be: cash it.
edits.after: Stormbringer disables his tower, but Nature's Grasp is 130s at 3000 range and roots your leap's exit — do not dive into a full-health Maokai.

edits.before: Level 2 stays yours as W's heal wins the trades through his sapling poke.
edits.after: Level 2 is his — Bramble Smash (7s) knocks you back out of every bite.

edits.before: Level 3 favours you: full combo all-in beats him while his mana lags.
edits.after: Level 3 is his: Twisted Advance roots you into sapling damage.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain yours since his damage can't threaten your health pool.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out — his Sap Magic heal answers your Maul re-bite.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours — R Stormbringer answers his all-in and out-bursts him.
edits.after: Level 6 is his — Nature's Grasp (130s) roots you from 3000 range.

edits.before: At 2+ items Maokai's full-tank build and CC make him an unkillable peel wall.
edits.after: At 2+ items your health and on-hit bites out-last his low damage output.

The two packets disagree. I followed the mirror per the do-not-fight-the-mirror rule, but a human should confirm which packet is authoritative before this ships — it is a six-row swing on a 50.75% matchup. Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' derived flag his description does not support (knockback and slow only); if real it would deny Stormbringer, so it is flagged rather than written.
